title: Direct Objects & Accusative Articles
cheatsheet:
## Stage 03: Direct Objects & Accusative Articles

**Structure:** `Subject` + `Conjugated Verb` + `Accusative Object`

**Case Focus:** Accusative Case (the direct object receiving the action).

**Rule:** Only **Masculine** articles change (`der` → `den`, `ein` → `einen`, `kein` → `keinen`). Feminine, Neuter, and Plural stay identical to their nominative (Stage 02) forms.

### Article Declension (Nominative vs. Accusative)

| Gender | Nominative | Accusative |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Masculine | der / ein / kein | **den / einen / keinen** |
| Feminine | die / eine / keine | die / eine / keine |
| Neuter | das / ein / kein | das / ein / kein |
| Plural | die / — / keine | die / — / keine |

### Sentence Frames
* `[Subject] + [Verb] + [Accusative Article + Noun]`
* Ich brauche **einen** Schlüssel. *(I need a key. — Masculine)*
* Du hast **eine** Taschenlampe. *(You have a flashlight. — Feminine)*
* Er liest **ein** Buch. *(He reads a book. — Neuter)*
* Wir kaufen **keine** Äpfel. *(We buy no apples. — Plural)*

### POS Tags Used
`PRON` pronoun · `VERB` conjugated verb · `DET` article (definite/indefinite/negative) · `NOUN` noun · `ADV` adverb (e.g. *not*)

sentences.english: They look for not a man.
You look for not a number.
You all see not a room.
They look for not a ticket.
